findings.trigger: Read routes/artifacts.py and docs/api/README.md: 'Four things narrow the credential, and each one is tested', the fourth being 'stored hashed'.
findings.wrong_outcome: No test asserts how the token is persisted. Replacing hash_token(token) with token in store.create_artifact_download_token keeps the whole suite green, so the coverage claim retires a risk nothing covers.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'hash_token|token_hash|plaintext' tests/integration/test_artifacts.py -> no output; the two ArtifactDownloadToken call sites in tests only seed an expired row.
findings.closure: tests/integration/test_artifacts.py::test_the_download_token_is_never_stored_in_the_clear, plus ::test_a_token_stops_at_the_projects_the_account_still_has for the untested '(or narrows)' half. Docstring rewritten to name each test.

findings.trigger: A client follows docs/api/README.md and reads android.signingFingerprint from the POST .../download-token response to verify the signer before the transfer.
findings.wrong_outcome: The field is absent. The mint handler returns eight scalar keys and no android block, and ArtifactDownloadGrant declares none, so the README contradicts both the code and the contract.
findings.evidence: Probe over the live endpoint: MINT KEYS: ['artifactId','contentType','downloadPath','expiresAt','sha256','sizeBytes','token','tokenType'].
findings.closure: Prose corrected: the fingerprint is on the list and the detail, and the mint carries only what a downloader needs.

findings.trigger: Generate a client from the OpenAPI document and GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/download for an APK recorded with contentType application/vnd.android.package-archive.
findings.wrong_outcome: Content-Type is the artifact's own media type, which is not among the types the 200/206 declare; the document also says elsewhere that Artifact.contentType is 'the media type the download is served with', so it states two different types for one response.
findings.closure: Declared as '*/*' with the reason inline; no contract test compares content types, which is why nothing caught it.

findings.trigger: A client generated from the document is configured with one bearerAuth credential (the session access token) and calls downloadArtifact.
findings.wrong_outcome: It attaches the session token, which this route refuses; every refusal here is deliberately the same 401, so the client's standard 401 interceptor refreshes the session and retries forever. bearerAuth's own description additionally promises 'an expired or revoked token is refused everywhere', which is false of this operation's credential.
findings.evidence: Probe dumped every operation's security: downloadArtifact -> [{'bearerAuth': []}], while tests/integration/test_artifacts.py::test_a_session_bearer_token_does_not_download asserts 401 for exactly that credential.
findings.closure: New artifactDownloadToken security scheme and DownloadTokenRejected response component; tests/contract/test_openapi_document.py::test_the_artifact_download_does_not_claim_the_session_credential and ::test_every_declared_security_scheme_is_used.

findings.trigger: Alice mints a download token, then signs out: POST /api/v1/auth/revoke with her access token (or with her refresh token).
findings.wrong_outcome: Revoke answers 200, the session token is dead (catalogue -> 401), and the download token still streams the bytes for the rest of its TTL - up to 3600s at the configured ceiling. Nothing can revoke it. Verbatim the failure routes/auth.py says the endpoint exists to prevent, and it contradicts docs/security.md 'revogacao vale para os dois transportes'.
findings.location: gateway/app/services/store.py:853-908 (both revoke paths); gateway/app/api/routes/artifacts.py:314-355; migrations/0008_artifacts.sql (no revocation state)
findings.evidence: Probe: revoke -> 200 {'accessTokensRevoked':1}; session after revoke -> 401; DOWNLOAD TOKEN AFTER SESSION REVOKE -> 200, full body. Reproduced independently by the second-caller lens on a separate app assembly.
findings.closure: store._revoke_artifact_download_tokens called from both revocation doors; tests/integration/test_auth.py::test_signing_out_kills_a_download_token_minted_before_it and ::test_revoking_by_refresh_token_also_kills_the_download_tokens. Both fail without the fix (verified by reverting).

findings.trigger: A client reports 'The stored content for this artifact is not available.' with a requestId; the operator greps the gateway log for it, as _content_missing's docstring instructs.
findings.wrong_outcome: Nothing is found. ApiError is rendered by install_error_handlers, which logs nothing, and the gateway has no access-log middleware, so the requestId maps to no record. That capability is the justification for not naming the artifact in the response.
findings.evidence: caplog at DEBUG over the whole request: every record was harness noise (aiosqlite driver echo, the httpx client). No gateway logger emitted anything and no record carried the request id.

findings.trigger: A programmer writing the ingestion endpoint reads ArtifactError's docstring: 'the store raises it and the route turns it into 400 validation_failed with a JSON Pointer'.
findings.wrong_outcome: There is no such conversion. No _planning_error equivalent and no exception handler exist for ArtifactError, so one reaching a request path renders as 500 internal_error and the authored field/code pointers never reach a client. The single except ArtifactError on a route converts it to 404.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'ArtifactError' gateway/ shows only the import and one except clause; ArtifactError.field/.code are read only inside tests.
findings.closure: Docstring rewritten to state that no endpoint accepts an artifact today, why the pointers exist anyway, and what the ingestion endpoint owes.

findings.trigger: Any reader or tool consulting docs/codemap.md for the signature of the new list endpoint.
findings.wrong_outcome: The map advertises list_artifacts(response, project, type, origin, cursor, limit, principal, session); the function takes seven parameters and no response. Same shape as the 2026-07-16 codemap advertising a require_scope that no longer existed.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'list_artifacts(' docs/codemap.md against sed -n '204,212p' of the route module; every other new codemap entry matched.
findings.closure: Regenerated with governancekit --root . map (root path normalized back to the canonical checkout).

findings.trigger: Any holder of a live download token sends Range: bytes=<4301 or more decimal digits>- to GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/download.
findings.wrong_outcome: 500 internal_error with retryable:true - inviting the client to repeat it - plus an unhandled_exception stack trace per request, where 4300 digits produce a correct 416. _RANGE_RE accepted an unbounded digit run and int() refuses past CPython's CVE-2020-10735 threshold.
findings.evidence: 4299 digits -> 416; 4300 -> 416; 4301 -> 500, with ValueError: Exceeds the limit (4300) for integer string conversion in the traceback.
findings.closure: Digit bound in the pattern (an over-long run is a malformed range, which the function already answers with None); tests/integration/test_artifacts.py::test_an_absurdly_long_range_is_not_a_five_hundred. Verified to fail without the fix.

findings.trigger: An operator upgrades an existing deployment and skips python3 scripts/apply_migrations.py.
findings.wrong_outcome: The gateway boots normally. Base.metadata.create_all runs one statement before check_schema and creates the three tables, so the guard sees them present: no boot failure naming 0008, none of its three indexes, no content_type default, and no schema_migrations row. docs/api/README.md, added by this delivery, promised the opposite.
findings.evidence: Booted the real app against a SQLite database at 0007: artifact tables present before boot NONE, BOOT succeeded, indexes after boot NONE, schema_migrations rows [].
findings.closure: Prose corrected in docs/api/README.md; tests/unit/test_schema_guard.py::test_required_tables_cannot_fire_at_boot_today pins it. The mechanism is pre-existing and affects every table-only migration, so changing it is escalated to the operator in docs/issues/011-artifacts-downloads-apk/RESUME.md rather than decided here (council.md section 1, the one-way door).

findings.trigger: The next author - concretely whoever writes the ingestion path - reads docs/api/README.md section 'Fields that must never ship' to learn what must not leave the server.
findings.wrong_outcome: The list names ProjectModel.path as 'the canonical trap' and says nothing about ArtifactModel.storage_path, while the migration, the model, the route module, the new README section and a test all cite that section as the authority forbidding it. The pointer's target does not contain the rule.
findings.location: docs/api/README.md:163-176, cited from migrations/0008_artifacts.sql:8, gateway/app/models/entities.py:206, docs/api/README.md:1124, tests/integration/test_artifacts.py:747, docs/required-reading.md:55
findings.evidence: grep for the section title finds seven citations; sed of lines 169-171 shows only ProjectModel.path, and git show 9ba4e7b -- docs/api/README.md never touches that section.

questions: nginx location /api/ sets no proxy_buffering off or proxy_max_temp_file_size, so a 60 MB APK spools through proxy_temp on the front-door host before the client sees the tail. Read off deploy/nginx/*.conf plus documented defaults; not measured, no nginx instance available.

migrations/0008_artifacts.sql is never applied against PostgreSQL in the suite. SQLite accepts references projects(id) against a non-existent table and PostgreSQL does not, so a Postgres-only defect in a future migration would not be caught. not reproduced: no PostgreSQL instance available.

The two 0008 indexes exist only in the .sql, not on the models, so every test and any create_all-first deployment runs the catalogue's ORDER BY without artifacts_project_id_created_at_idx. Deliberate (migrations own indexes) or an omission?

The expired-download-token sweep fires only on mint. Correctness is unaffected because get_artifact_download_token re-checks expiry, but on a deployment where minting stops the credential table stops being pruned - the unboundedness the sweep's own docstring says it exists to avoid.

Is bare SHA-256 (shared.security.hash_token) the intended storage for this credential? It matches create_oauth_access_token and the token is 48 CSPRNG bytes, so it is defensible; security-standards.md section 11 mandates a slow KDF for passwords and is silent on high-entropy bearer tokens. Worth pinning in writing now that there is a second table of them.
